      <title>One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (<a href="https://www.unfpa.org/latest?_gl=1*qgl8yd*_up*MQ..*_gs*MQ..&amp;gclid=Cj0KCQiAtvXXBhC2ARIsAJc8SUT_aKqck2yVoC8vNqJ6FDghCWHDwCXcKD3yGJ9fmgqTGSh0z0LaYAcaAvlMEALw_wcB&amp;gbraid=0AAAAAoaU5jLrFra9lcVEXtmHPvgYu0nsj">UNFPA</a>) published on Thursday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court</link>
      <description><p>A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza</p><p>Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay</a>, if the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/15/myanmar-rohingya-genocide-icj">court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide</a> against the Rohingya.</p><p>The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans</link>
      <description><p>Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans</p><p>The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.</p><p>The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/17/egypt-eu-deal-refugees-mediterranean">promised by Ursula von der Leyen</a>, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/pete-hegseth-venezuela-nicolas-maduro-military</link>
      <description><p>Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago</p><p>Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.</p><p>Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/pete-hegseth-venezuela-nicolas-maduro-military">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/19/mike-lynch-superyacht-bayesian-vulnerability-to-high-winds-report</link>
      <description><p>Bayesian, which sank off Sicily killing seven including tech tycoon, had not been fully assessed, say investigators</p><p>The superyacht Bayesian, which sank in a storm off Sicily killing seven people including the tech tycoon Mike Lynch and his teenage daughter, was vulnerable to knockdown but crew were not aware as it had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down, the final report from the UK’s Marine Accident Investigations Branch (MAIB) has said.</p><p>The 56-metre (184ft) vessel was anchored near the fishing port of Porticello when <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2024/oct/04/mike-lynch-died-from-drowning-bayesian-yacht-inquest-hears">it sank during a violent storm</a> shortly before dawn on 19 August 2024.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/19/mike-lynch-superyacht-bayesian-vulnerability-to-high-winds-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/19/kerch-bridge-crimea-russia-attacked-again-ukraine</link>
      <description><p>Assessment of damage is underway, days after two attacks that destroyed road section of key bridge across Kerch strait linking annexed peninsula to Russia</p><p>A key bridge connecting annexed Crimea to Russia has been attacked again, a Russian-appointed regional governor has said, two days after Ukrainian strikes caused serious damage to it.</p><p>“Following a new attack on the Crimean Bridge, traffic has been temporarily halted. All relevant services are on site and at work. An assessment of the damage is under way,” Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, wrote on Telegram. The Russian transport ministry said on Thursday that no one was wounded in the attack and that train services across it had been halted.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/19/kerch-bridge-crimea-russia-attacked-again-ukraine">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/eu-loan-ukraine-cash-crisis-defences-von-der-leyen-kyiv</link>
      <description><p>Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea </p><p>The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues.</p><p>Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/18/eu-uk-reset-summit-talks-burnham-brexit</link>
      <description><p>Diplomats say piecemeal approach of resets is coming to an end and Europe wants clarity on whether Britain wants to reverse its exit</p><p>The EU will shut the door to discussions with Andy Burnham about the UK’s longer-term relationship with the bloc until the government has decided whether it wants to proceed with reversing Brexit, diplomats have said.</p><p>European capitals are also warning they have reached the end of the line for piecemeal “reset” summits with the UK and want the prime minister to focus on his next steps domestically before they proceed.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/18/eu-uk-reset-summit-talks-burnham-brexit">Continue reading...</a></description>

France will seek European-level sanctions against Iran in response to cyberattacks on hundreds of supermarket fridges, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Tuesday, after accusing Tehran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating the October sabotage. Iran's foreign ministry said the accusations were "baseless and one-sided".

rumours</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261110-macrons-file-new-defamation-lawsuit-against-us-podcaster-over-transgender-rumours</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efe09190-dcbf-11f1-9487-5f60e87d1ec6</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 04:33:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg">© Abdul Saboor, POOL/AFP/File</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-top-contemporary-french-artist-christian-boltanski-dies-aged-76</link><description>
Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>
Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2534ffb8-8980-11ec-8ce4-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 12:31:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sharon GAFFNEY</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says world leaders have made 'stupid' comments on France riots based on fake AI videos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261021-macron-says-world-leaders-have-made-stupid-comments-on-france-riots-based-on-fake-ai-videos</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>
Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4e47fa4-88f4-11ec-97bf-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 10:43:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png">© FMM Graphic Studio</source><dc:creator>Tracy MCNICOLL</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teen wounds headmaster and teacher after opening fire at French school</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-french-police-arrest-14-year-old-after-two-teaching-staff-wounded-by-hunting-rifle-fire</link><description>
Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">de062bda-c61f-11f1-828c-2d5a86616301</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg">© Lou Benoist, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France 2022: The Choice</category><title>Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/france-2022-the-campaign/20220207-battle-for-the-far-right-zemmour-le-pen-fight-to-steal-each-other-s-thunder</link><description>
As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ecf0724-8861-11ec-862b-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Feb 2022 22:00:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PERELMAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261011-a-profile-of-rapha%C3%ABl-glucksmann-the-man-who-wants-to-be-french-president</link><description>
Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential elections, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 00:20:12 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>France rejects 'absurd' Russian claims of direct involvement in Ukraine war</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-france-rejects-absurd-russian-claims-of-direct-involvement-in-ukraine-war</link><description>
The French government on Tuesday dismissed Russian accusations that France is directly involved in the war in Ukraine, following an RFI investigation which revealed a small number of French soldiers have been carrying out training and equipment maintenance missions on Ukrainian territory. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ffdd448e-e346-11f1-831b-65a66bd770f6</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:39:09 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg">AFP - BERTRAND GUAY</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French interior minister accused of 'exaggerating' police protest injury figures</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-french-interior-minister-accused-of-exaggerating-police-protest-injury-figures</link><description>
A group of lawyers have called for an investigation into French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez who they accuse of "spreading false information" about the number of injuries suffered by law enforcement officers since the start of the current protest movement, which they say was used "to justify a disproportionate use of force" against high school protesters.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">294b16e6-e335-11f1-af18-6757e9484dfb</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:09:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg">AFP - SEBASTIEN BOZON</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'We weren't afraid of the future': France's student protests today and in May '68</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-we-weren-t-afraid-of-the-future-france-s-student-protests-today-and-in-may-68</link><description>
As students across France continue demonstrating against conditions in schools, the movement has drawn inevitable comparisons with the biggest student protests in the country's history – those of May 1968. While this date remains a rallying cry for many young French people, they are calling for change in a world that has altered profoundly in the past 58 years.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">457488e8-dceb-11f1-88f8-bd68fc553891</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:01:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg">© JACQUES MARIE / AFP </source><dc:creator>Jessica Phelan</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Lower turnout at latest French cost-of-living protests, but anger still raw</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-lower-turnout-at-latest-french-cost-of-living-protests-but-anger-still-raw</link><description>
Tens of thousands of people demonstrated across France on Tuesday in a fresh nationwide public sector strike over pay and the cost of living. Although turnout was lower than at previous protests, anger remained strong – with many demonstrators also voicing fears about the far right coming to power in the 2027 presidential election.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8f4305e2-dd0b-11f1-ad88-012109f6bc5c</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 06:05:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG">REUTERS/Pascal Rosssignol</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students demonstrate solidarity in the fight for better schools</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-students-demonstrate-solidarity-in-the-fight-for-better-schools</link><description>
It began as a protest over crumbling classrooms and missing teachers, but France's student movement is now challenging the political establishment to give young people more of a say in decisions about their future. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f19af422-dc5f-11f1-a6cf-03231484c166</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 21:55:52 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg">AP Photo/Nicolas Garriga - Nicolas Garriga</source><dc:creator>Alison Hird</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French student protests continue amid deadlock over education reforms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-student-protests-continue-amid-deadlock-over-education-reforms</link><description>
Students and teachers are planning a new day of strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday, as talks with the government remain deadlocked, nearly two months after the start of protests by high school and university students.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37288fa8-dcd4-11f1-aace-7ff548d44c0a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 06:59:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner joins race for French presidency</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-olympic-judo-champion-teddy-riner-joins-race-for-french-presidency</link><description>
France's five-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner announced on Monday that he would run in next year's presidential election, expressing concern particularly over "the rise of the far right".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ff9ac7be-dc3c-11f1-a6ee-d528d7ed3f40</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:44:42 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/24e10c34-dc35-11f1-9eaf-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26313423095961.jpg">© AP - Michel Euler</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM's move to increase minimum wage fails to convince unions</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261109-french-pm-s-move-to-increase-minimum-wage-fails-to-convince-unions</link><description>
The French government on Monday announced a 1.6 percent increase in the national minimum wage, alongside a series of measures aimed at easing cost of living pressures. However, the decision fell well short of the demands of trade unions, who have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1fb23d3e-dc42-11f1-9f6d-714e057b766f</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 17:36:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/391ca27a-db78-11f1-86b0-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26311499885536.jpg">© Emma Da Silva/AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/18/howard-lutnick-nvidia-cantor-fitzgerald</link>
      <description><p>Democratic lawmakers ask if commerce secretary favored Nvidia to enrich his adult children and Cantor Fitzgerald</p><p>The US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, faces mounting questions over his handling of the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nvidia">Nvidia</a> affair as Democratic lawmakers demand answers over his family firm’s vast stake in the tech company.</p><p>Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Lutnick ran for decades before joining the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-administration">Trump administration</a>, held shares in Nvidia worth “hundreds of millions of dollars” while Lutnick made key decisions affecting the tech firm’s ability to operate, according to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/democrats">Democrats</a> on three key congressional committees.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/18/howard-lutnick-nvidia-cantor-fitzgerald">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/nvidia-third-quarter-revenue-jensen-huang</link>
      <description><p>Company issues first earnings report after ouster of CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spy</p><p>Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday. Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster.</p><p>Nvidia announced the same day that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago. The third-quarter earnings report comes just days after the world’s most valuable chip company saw the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns">ouster of Huang</a> over allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with his own employees.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/nvidia-third-quarter-revenue-jensen-huang">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/17/trump-bbc-deposition-delay</link>
      <description><p>President, who had agreed to sit for deposition in October but backed out, must now appear by 22 January</p><p>Donald Trump has been granted a temporary delay before he must give a witness statement in his $10bn defamation lawsuit against the BBC.</p><p>In late October, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/22/trump-bbc-lawsuit-deposition-discovery">Enjoliqué Lett, a federal magistrate judge, gave Trump a firm 11 December deadline</a> to sit for a deposition by lawyers representing the BBC in his lawsuit against the British broadcaster. If he failed to do so by that date, he could be subject to penalties up to dismissal of the case, the judge warned.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/17/trump-bbc-deposition-delay">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Deutsche Bank dismissed warnings about dealings with risky clients, reports claim</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim</link>
      <description><p>International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profits</p><p>Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate.</p><p>A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2019/apr/17/deutsche-bank-faces-action-over-20bn-russian-money-laundering-scheme">been caught being used to launder billions of dollars</a> for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/17/deutsche-bank-dimissed-warnings-risky-clients-reports-claim">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Americans relying on heating oil brace for harsh winter: ‘We’re often cold in our own home’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/16/heating-oil-price-increase-winter</link>
      <description><p>Surge in prices is forcing many to cut back on spending, with a projected 21% increase in costs of those households</p><p>Millions of homeowners in the US will pay hundreds of dollars more this winter to heat their homes as rising energy prices have pushed up the price of heating oil.</p><p>The US Energy Information Administration <a href="https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=68264&amp;utm_medium=email">projects</a> households that use heating oil can expect to pay 21% more this year compared with last winter, with warmer temperatures expected to partly offset price increases.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/16/heating-oil-price-increase-winter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Farewell to Elon Musk’s Cybertruck. Has any car ever been more repellent? | Arwa Mahdawi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent</link>
      <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/manchester-united-infamous-1974-relegation-is-a-warning-from-history</link>
      <description><p>It may have been a different era, but the 1970s contain salutary lessons for a club in serious decline once again</p><p>In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years.</p><p>Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/manchester-united-infamous-1974-relegation-is-a-warning-from-history">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Veerle Buurman scrambles late WCL winner to push blunt Chelsea past PSG</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/chelsea-paris-saint-germain-womens-champions-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Chelsea were made to work hard for three Champions League points against a resilient Paris Saint-Germain side but their patience paid off, Veerle Buurman squeezing the ball in at the near post to put them, temporarily at least, at the top of the table in the league phase.</p><p>Buurman had stolen the show in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/chelsea-manchester-city-womens-super-league-match-report">Chelsea’s defeat of Manchester City</a> at the weekend, coming on 12 minutes in and nullifying Khadija Shaw’s threat to be named player of the match, and she was the hero under the lights with Chelsea doing everything but score prior to her goal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/chelsea-paris-saint-germain-womens-champions-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/leicester-city-bc-game-porn-star-eva-elfie-sponsorship</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Cryptocurrency casino made Eva Elfie a brand ambassador</p></li><li><p>Club end deal early citing ‘differing commercial priorities’</p></li></ul><p>Leicester City have ditched their front-of-shirt sponsor, BC Game, after the cryptocurrency casino’s partnership with a porn actor sparked a fan backlash. BC Game, an offshore company registered in Belize <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/08/premier-league-clubs-sponsorship-advertising-deals-unlicensed-gambling-companies-uk-government">that is unlicensed to operate in the UK</a>, had been Leicester’s main sponsor since 2024.</p><p>This month BC Game named Eva Elfie a brand ambassador, leading the Foxes Trust, Leicester’s supporters’ trust, to highlight the “devastating impacts” caused by gambling and pornography. On Wednesday the club said they prematurely ended their agreement with the online betting firm after they “recognised our differing commercial priorities”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/leicester-city-bc-game-porn-star-eva-elfie-sponsorship">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>US women’s head coach won Olympics in 2024</p></li><li><p>Hayes enjoyed trophy-laden tenure at Chelsea</p></li></ul><p>The US women’s national team head coach, Emma Hayes, said she was “confident in the group that is being put together” to select her next counterpart for the men’s team – a group that includes&nbsp;her.</p><p>Speaking after <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/uswnt-squad-concacaf-w-championship-world-cup-qualifier">announcing her team’s squad</a> for the ­Concacaf championship and World Cup qualifier, Hayes shed light for the first time on her role in searching for Mauricio Pochettino’s replacement after the Argentinian <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/mauricio-pochettino-confirmed-manchester-united-usa">decamped to Manchester United</a>. US Soccer had previously said Hayes – alongside the federation CEO, JT Batson, the chief operating officer, Dan Helfrich, and Oguchi Onyewu, the vice-president of sporting – would assist with the search.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/emma-hayes-usmnt-head-coach-hiring-process">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/netflix-fox-2030-world-cup-television-rights</link>
      <description><p>The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry</p><p>The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.</p><p>Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/netflix-fox-2030-world-cup-television-rights">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘An honour’: Pochettino up for challenge of leading Manchester United revival</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/mauricio-pochettino-arrives-manchester-united-head-coach-premier-league</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>New head coach faces tough opening match at Anfield</p></li><li><p>‘It’s a big challenge but at the same time it’s adrenaline’</p></li></ul><p>Mauricio Pochettino said it was “an honour” and “a privilege” <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/here-manchester-united-go-again-taking-the-two-ronnies-route-to-hiring-a-new-boss">to be the new Manchester United head coach</a> after arriving in England on Wednesday.</p><p>Pochettino flew from Cincinnati to Manchester overnight <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/usmnt-haiti-nations-league-mauricio-pochettino">after overseeing the USA beating Haiti</a> in his final game in charge. His right-hand man, Jesús Pérez, the goalkeeping coach Toni Jiménez and the fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino, who continues to work with his father, have already taken training with those not on international duty.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/mauricio-pochettino-arrives-manchester-united-head-coach-premier-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/fifa-hydration-breaks-2030-world-cup-tv-right-documents</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Controversial breaks were financial boon for broadcasters</p></li><li><p>Fifa flags possible benefits but says no decision made</p></li></ul><p>Fifa’s tender documents for TV rights for the 2030 World Cup include a provision for broadcasters<strong> </strong>to sell adverts during hydration breaks in a strong indication <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/26/fifa-unites-the-world-in-anger-at-hydration-breaks-aka-ad-breaks">the controversial ­stoppages</a> will be retained.</p><p>A three-minute break midway through each half was introduced for the first time at all 104 matches at last summer’s World Cup in the interests of player welfare, a radical move that also provided a commercial boon for broadcasters, particularly the rights holders in the United States, Fox Sports and Telemundo.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/fifa-hydration-breaks-2030-world-cup-tv-right-documents">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Overlap, underlap or sit back? How Premier League teams use their full-backs</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst</link>
      <description><p>The role of full-back has changed massively in recent years. We analyse how all 20 sides are approaching the position</p><p>By <a href="https://theanalyst.com/">Opta Analyst</a></p><p>Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.</p><p>Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Jack Grealish recalls a golden age of mavericks – but football has moved on</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on</link>
      <description><p>Everton forward has magical talent and popularity to burn, but has come up against hard reality of the modern game</p><p>Thomas Tuchel has never called up the player he once claimed to love “everything about”. The reason for Jack Grealish’s omission from Tuchel’s first England squad in March 2025 was given as “he simply has no rhythm”.</p><p>Catch a falling star? Last month Grealish <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/29/jack-grealish-axed-everton-breach-club-discipline-newcastle-caraboao-cup">was suspended by Everton</a> for three matches after “a breach of club discipline”. Suggestions his loan from Manchester City might be cancelled were calmed by David Moyes. Last week, Grealish played in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Derby before issuing an Instagram statement: “I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.” Amid tabloid tales of karaoke nights and extended socialising, how close is the former boy wonder, now 31, to blowing it?</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT time will be remembered fondly, but it wasn’t transformational</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/pochettino-usmnt-manchester-united</link>
      <description><p>The incoming Manchester United manager improved the US team’s culture and competitiveness, but could not bring about sea change in two years</p><p>In a theater high up in a midtown Manhattan skyscraper built from lots of glass, a highlight reel played to deafening music. And then, on “a monumental day for US Soccer”, federation president, Cindy Parlow Cone, announced they had bagged their man, Mauricio Pochettino, to become the highest-profile United States manager in the men’s national team’s history.</p><p>Pochettino held court for three-quarters of an hour in his signature blend of Spanglish before the assembled media and a grab bag of sponsors. Then he recorded some TV hits. And after that, in a bit of accidental prescience, he went off to record a podcast with Gary Neville.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/pochettino-usmnt-manchester-united">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘When I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West’: the two lives of Bromley footballer Omar Sowunmi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/omar-sowunmi-bromley-footballer-model-kanye-west</link>
      <description><p>Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career</p><p>“I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds.</p><p>Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/omar-sowunmi-bromley-footballer-model-kanye-west">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/uswnt-squad-concacaf-w-championship-world-cup-qualifier</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Win over El Salvador would qualify US for Brazil 2027</p></li><li><p>Naomi Girma misses squad due to injury</p></li><li><p>Sam Coffey returns after injury absence</p></li></ul><p>In the two years since the Paris Olympics, Emma Hayes has thoroughly tested fresh faces and new combinations, gathering a considerable amount of data about the US women’s national team. It’s been a thorough process, with 33 players earning their first caps since Hayes assumed the post, to bring her roster of options to 61 players.</p><p>At last, the main event is nearing. On 27 November, the United States will enter the Concacaf W Championship with a clear objective: beat El Salvador. Winning the whole thing is nice, of course, and the USWNT have done so in nine of the tournament’s 11 installments to date. But by far the most important game on that journey is the first one, that quarter-final date with clear stakes: overcome El Salvador, or rely on a playoff to reach next summer’s World Cup.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/uswnt-squad-concacaf-w-championship-world-cup-qualifier">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Haaland’s late penalty grabs Norway last-eight spot</p></li><li><p>Parrott penalties help Republic of Ireland secure playoff</p></li></ul><p>A wonder strike from Justin Devenny earned <strong>Northern Ireland </strong>top spot in Nations League Group B2 and promotion to the top tier of the competition.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wales-portugal-nations-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese Football Federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards.</p><p>For Wales, a Nations League relegation playoff double-header awaits in March, with Slovenia, Hungary, Republic of Ireland or Bosnia and Herzegovina – who knocked them out of World Cup qualifying this year – all potential opponents in Friday’s draw in Switzerland. Afterwards Craig Bellamy stressed the importance of keeping elite company to accelerate improvement but reiterated that he will not be in the job beyond Euro 2028, after which his contract expires.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/wales-portugal-nations-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more</p><ul><li><p><a href="mailto:knowledge@theguardian.com"><strong>Mail us</strong></a><strong> with all of your questions and answers</strong></p></li></ul><p><strong>“The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,”</strong> writes Bogdan Kotarlic. <strong>“Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?”</strong></p><p>The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles.       <title>‘The game is in danger’: PFA head Maheta Molango on Fifa, Infantino and football’s future</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/pfa-maheta-molango-interview-fifa-gianni-infantino-interview</link>
      <description><p>At a potentially critical juncture for football, the PFA’s chief executive talks about the organisation, wider fears in the game and why the Folarin Balogun affair was ‘scandalous’</p><p>After five years in charge of the Professional Footballers’ Association, what has Maheta Molango learned? “The game is in danger,” the 44-year-old says. “I’ve learned that the game I loved and led me to first play and then advise and then lead a club and today to lead the PFA, is in danger because it is being forgotten.”</p><p>In 2026, with football ubiquitous on all platforms, with a World Cup that generated $15bn (£11.4bn) in revenue, and with attendances across the English pyramid growing year on year, it may seem hard to imagine forgetting about the game. But Molango’s unique perspective as head of the players’ union for England and Wales observes a different picture; one where the future of the sport is being determined not by what will maintain its popularity, but what will make the most money.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/pfa-maheta-molango-interview-fifa-gianni-infantino-interview">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/sport">Sport</category>

      <title>Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes</link>
      <description><p>A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation</p><p>“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.</p><p>The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jul/14/diego-maradona-argentina-world-cup">Argentina’s football folklore</a> are spliced with excellent archive material.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/reliving-the-drama-england-and-argentina-stars-watch-1986-classic-with-fresh-eyes">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pocognoli’s aspiration for how Scotland must play is in danger of becoming unworkable</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland</link>
      <description><p>The 4-0 debacle against Switzerland has added to the tactical concerns about the head coach’s suitability, just six games into the job</p><p>The Scottish Football Association can only cling to a lesson from the past when assessing a worrying international window. Steve Clarke was beleaguered during his early games in charge. Successive 4-0 defeats by Belgium and Russia in 2019 left Clarke with the sense he should have stayed in club management. A revival meant Clarke led his country to three out of four tournaments.</p><p>There are, however, fundamental differences between the story of Clarke and that being delivered by Sébastien Pocognoli. Clarke was a pragmatist, whose decades in coaching suggested he had the wherewithal to revive Scotland. Pocognoli, six games into his tenure, is in danger of lurching into the territory of dreamy ideologue whose aspiration for how Scotland must play is unworkable. The meek nature of Scotland’s collapse in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/switzerland-scotland-nations-league-match-report">4-0 loss to a second-string Switzerland</a> was lamentable. The Belgian’s assessment, with overpraise a key theme, raised eyebrows.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/sebastien-pocognoli-scotland-nations-league-switzerland">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham</link>
      <description><p>Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France </p><p>There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.</p><p>Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal Under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/nov/04/slavia-prague-arsenal-champions-league-match-report">at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days</a>, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/mar/14/arsenal-everton-premier-league-match-report">Premier League’s youngest goalscorer</a>. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/max-dowman-england-under-21s-record-jude-bellingham">Continue reading...</a></description>
